classification.difficultyReason: Adapt the explicitly referenced taught proof: identify two alternate-angle equalities and equal opposite sides, establish triangle congruence, then infer equality of the matching diagonal segments.

content.prompt: In the diagram to the right, $XYZW$ is a parallelogram. $M$ is the point of intersection of $XZ$ and $YW$. Prove that $XM=ZM$, as presented earlier.

spec.description: Unshaded parallelogram with single parallel arrows on XY and WZ, double parallel arrows on YZ and XW, and red dashed diagonals meeting at a red point M. Ordinary source-blue outlines and arrows become house black.
spec.mathematics: Vertices run X, Y, Z, W around the boundary. XY is parallel to WZ; YZ is parallel to XW. Diagonals XZ and YW meet at M. No equal-length marks or supplied answers.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied geometry, parallel marks, diagonals and point labels are visible.

answer.short:
$XM=ZM$.

$\triangle XYM\equiv\triangle ZWM$ by AAS, so their matching sides $XM$ and $ZM$ are equal.
answer.worked:
In triangles $XYM$ and $ZWM$:

$\angle YXM=\angle WZM$ (alternate angles, $XY\parallel WZ$).

$\angle XYM=\angle ZWM$ (alternate angles, $XY\parallel WZ$).

$XY=ZW$ (opposite sides of parallelogram $XYZW$).

Therefore $\triangle XYM\equiv\triangle ZWM$ (AAS).

Hence $XM=ZM$ (matching sides of congruent triangles).
